newsitem.title: USA: NY law school deans back City bar on pay-to-play.
newsitem.headline: NY law school deans back City bar on pay-to-play.

text.p: The deans of 11 New York law schools announced their support for the New York City bar's recommended ban on pay-to-play by municipal bond lawyers.

Among those endorsing the controversial policy adopted last year by the Association of the Bar of the City of New York were David Leebron of Columbia University School of Law, John Feerick of Fordham University School of Law, Daan Braveman of Syracuse University College of Law, and Richard Ottinger of Pace University School of Law.

The deans said in a one-page letter to the Association, that they endorse "in principle" the proposed rule for adoption by the the New York State court system and by the American Bar Association. They said they do not necessarily endorse "each detail" of the proposal.

The City bar's rule would bar muni lawyers that solicit or make contributions to municipal clients, including some PAC contributions, from engaging in bond business for two years with those governments.
The ABA's influential standing committee on ethics has voted to oppose adoption of the measure by ABA delegates meeting this summer.
